NVDA.headline: Chip sector weakens amid AI worries; RTX 5090 supply questions
NVDA.summary: NVIDIA shares fell 1.43% today, though they remain up 16.87% over the year. Coverage points to wider AI-related jitters, including debt strain at CoreWeave, Oracle and SoftBank and a sector-wide selloff. Nvidia's Jeff Fisher denied reports that the RTX 5090 is being discontinued, saying it will keep shipping despite tight supply.

MSFT.headline: Shares slip as OpenAI faces state lawsuits and EU cloud law study
MSFT.summary: Microsoft shares fell 1.93% today, although they are up 6.29% over the month. Eight US states have sued OpenAI over alleged harms to children, and a lobby-funded study estimates the EU's proposed cloud sovereignty law could cost €115bn. A report says Microsoft has cancelled an unannounced Fallout game, but this is unconfirmed by the company.

AAPL.headline: App Store rules tightened on nudify apps; EE sets iPhone Handoff pricing
AAPL.summary: Apple shares rose 0.43% today and are up 36.14% over the year. Apple updated App Review Guidelines to target AI apps that generate non-consensual intimate imagery. EE has published UK pricing for iPhone Handoff, free on its top plan and £5 a month on others, with Apple saying the feature arrives by year-end. Canada's C-22 encryption bill and an unconfirmed report of an LG smart home partnership also feature in coverage.

GOOGL.headline: Shares fall as Universal Cart rolls out and antitrust talks continue
GOOGL.summary: Alphabet shares fell 2.47% today, though they are up 34.46% over the year. Google has begun rolling out Universal Cart in the US, a shopping hub across Search, Chrome and Gemini. Reports say the DOJ is discussing a settlement with Apple in an antitrust case, and a California datacentre project linked to interest from Google is facing legal challenges, which Google says it is not involved in.

AMZN.headline: Shares fall despite reports of AI chip sales and new Bee wearables
AMZN.summary: Amazon shares fell 1.87% today, though they are up 17.35% over the year. Coverage includes an unverified report that Amazon may sell around $8bn of Nvidia chips to investors, plus reports of another AI acquisition and an automation initiative for delivery stations. Amazon launched two Bee AI wearables, priced at $74.99 and $99.99, raising privacy questions.

META.headline: Shares drop 3.72% after data breach and scraping terms change
META.summary: Meta shares fell 3.72% today, and are up 3.96% over the month. Meta says hackers took code and data on about 1,500 people, mostly US-based employees, after accessing GitHub repositories. It also removed commercial-terms language that critics said could allow scraping of news sites for AI training, and says robots.txt preferences still apply. Coverage also notes that Meta's upcoming earnings are seen as a test for AI spending confidence.

AVGO.headline: Shares fall 4.52% as chip index posts longest losing streak since 2008
AVGO.summary: Broadcom shares fell 4.52% today and are down 5.34% over the month. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has recorded its longest losing streak since 2008, reflecting worries about AI. Broadcom is also among large US companies pushing back against proposed rules for tokenised stocks.

TSLA.headline: Second-generation Roadster unveiled with delayed 2028 production
TSLA.summary: Tesla shares fell 2.13% today and are down 19.26% over the year. The company showed its redesigned Roadster at SpaceX's Texas site, with production now slated for 2028 and reservations at $50,000 or $250,000. The FAA says it is not an aircraft, and analysts describe it as a halo product rather than a revenue driver. Coverage also includes Musk's political donations and comments on AI and US debt.

TSM.headline: Record profit, cautious 2027 outlook; China and Taiwan export curbs
TSM.summary: TSMC reported a record third-quarter net profit of NT$763.1bn, up 69% year on year, and expects 2026 dollar revenue growth of about 44%. Chairman C.C. Wei warned of pressure in consumer and price-sensitive markets and said the company is being prudent about 2027, though AI demand still exceeds supply. Taiwan is tightening export controls on AI servers and advanced chips, and China is drafting export licensing rules for AI technologies. Shares are down 2.28% today and 4.1% over one month, though up 39.83% over one year.

BRK-B.headline: Berkshire adds $330m to Bending Spoons stake
BRK-B.summary: Berkshire Hathaway has agreed to buy 10 million new Bending Spoons shares at $33 each, a $330m private placement, bringing its total investment to about $930m and a stake of roughly 4%. Mizuho analysts called it a vote of confidence in the company's model, and the deal still needs closing conditions and an SEC filing. Berkshire shares are up 1.21% today and 4.48% over one month, with a one-year gain of 8.04%.

LLY.headline: No major news right now
LLY.summary: There is no major news right now for Eli Lilly. The shares are up 0.43% today and 9.08% over one month, and up 56.57% over one year. The stock trades at $1,257.03, within its 52-week range of $793.82 to $1,292.65.

JPM.headline: Bank tax talk, bill yields and Fed call in focus
JPM.summary: Reports say John Healey may raise taxes on UK banks in the forthcoming Budget, with the IMF reportedly urging a focus on pensions or welfare instead, and UBS warning that higher bank taxes would raise mortgage costs. In the US, Treasury-bill yields have risen, with an eight-week auction clearing at 4.05% on record-low demand, while MarketWatch argues this month's Fed decision is closer than markets expect. Shares are up 1.25% today but down 2.75% over one month, and up 14.17% over one year.

WMT.headline: Google Universal Cart adds Walmart; Kroger cuts jobs
WMT.summary: Google has begun rolling out Universal Cart in the US, letting shoppers buy from retailers including Walmart across Search, Chrome and Gemini. Separately, Kroger plans to cut about 3,000 corporate roles over three years, citing technology and simplification. Several websites, including Amazon and JPMorgan, are restricting AI shopping agents, which could limit agent-based shopping. Walmart shares are up 0.8% today and 11.26% over one month, and up 10.28% over one year.

V.headline: No major news right now
V.summary: There is no major news right now for Visa. The shares are up 0.72% today and 8.83% over one month, and up 17.76% over one year. The stock trades at $402.61, near the top of its 52-week range of $293.89 to $404.74.

ORCL.headline: Debt strains across AI borrowers draw scrutiny
ORCL.summary: A New York Times Business piece highlights debt trouble at CoreWeave, Oracle and SoftBank, raising questions about wider strain in the AI data centre build-out. Related reporting says CoreWeave's debt has reached distress levels. Oracle shares are down 4.64% today, 14.85% over one month and 55.98% over one year, trading near the bottom of their 52-week range.

MA.headline: No major news right now
MA.summary: There is no major news right now for Mastercard. The shares are up 0.18% today and 9.14% over one month, and up 10.06% over one year. The stock trades at $617.42, close to its 52-week high of $622.49.

XOM.headline: Higher refining margins could add $4.5B to Q3 earnings
XOM.summary: ExxonMobil told investors in an 8-K filing that higher third-quarter refining margins could lift downstream profit by about $4.5 billion, on top of $4.1 billion from refining in the second quarter. Brent crude reached $110 a barrel for the first time since May, and the shares rose 2.46% today and 59.46% over the past year, near the top of their 52-week range. Reports also cite a US move to soften its stance on Russian oil sanctions, though the specific measures are unclear.

NFLX.headline: Netflix names Peter Rice content chief ahead of Q3 results
NFLX.summary: Netflix has named former Disney TV chairman Peter Rice as chief content officer, replacing Bela Bajaria, days after cutting about 6% of its workforce. The company reports fiscal third-quarter results on Tuesday, and the streamer has said growth is slower than it would like. The shares fell 2.86% today and are down 41.19% over the past year, trading near the lower end of their 52-week range. A UK proposal to extend the BBC licence fee to streaming services is reported but unconfirmed.

COST.headline: No major news right now
COST.summary: There is no major news right now for Costco. The shares rose 1.13% today and are up 10.65% over the past month, and trade within their 52-week range of 844.06 to 1096.5.

JNJ.headline: No major news right now
JNJ.summary: There is no major news right now for Johnson & Johnson. The shares rose 0.9% today but are down 5.43% over the past month, while still up 32.26% over the past year.
